issues.description: Extraction unconditionally requires data/stories/manifest.json and story files, but the repo does not include them, so the advertised tiny demo fails from a fresh checkout.
The only end-to-end test currently fails because required source data is absent.
Documented tiny demo commands are not reproducible with the checked-in repository state.
A PCA variance threshold of 0 is accepted but still returns one component, so users cannot disable neutral-PC projection via config.
Validation trusts vector artifacts without checking backend, model, layer count, d_model, or emotion compatibility against the current config.
Preference steering also trusts vector artifacts without compatibility checks, allowing mismatched configs to produce crashes or invalid results.
If configured emotions are not present in the built-in scenario list, np.stack is called on an empty list instead of raising a clear validation error.
Single-emotion validation leaves off_diagonal empty and records NaN summary metrics instead of rejecting the run.
Config values are cast but not validated, so empty emotions, zero topics, negative token_start, invalid layer fractions, and bad steering strengths fail later and unclearly.
Extraction assumes at least one story and will crash on min(start_positions) or stories[0] for empty datasets.
HuggingFace model/tokenizer downloads are unpinned by revision, making results non-reproducible and increasing supply-chain risk.
HuggingFace activation extraction has no truncation or max-length handling, so long stories can exceed context limits or cause memory failures.
The generic hf backend assumes a Gemma/Llama-style self.model.model.layers layout, so steering breaks on many AutoModelForCausalLM architectures.
When offset mappings are unavailable, activity steering falls back to every prompt token, contradicting the intended activity-token-only intervention.
Integration coverage only targets tiny mode and does not exercise the default HuggingFace backend, artifact mismatch handling, or invalid config paths.
Dependencies are lower-bound-only with no lockfile or constraints, weakening reproducibility for numerical outputs and model behavior.
Generated demo artifacts are checked in even though their source corpus is absent, leaving stale outputs that cannot currently be regenerated.
